pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headmaster
Brighton College Prep Handcross is a leading co-educational prep and boarding school in Sussex for children aged 2–13. We believe childhood is precious and want our pupils to enjoy this special time for as long as possible, within an environment that offers a wide range of stimulating opportunities for growth and development, both inside and outside the classroom. Our school is purposeful, ambitious, forward-thinking and most importantly of all, it is kind. Set in 52 acres of idyllic West Sussex countryside, we offer an exciting, bright and buzzing family school, where we are well known for our welcoming atmosphere, high academic standards, outstanding teaching and exceptional care for every child. We offer full, weekly and part-time boarding in our beautiful, home-from-home boarding house.
I would love to welcome you to our school so that you can see and feel the magic of Brighton College Prep Handcross for yourselves.
Jonnie BesleyHeadmaster
Who We Are
We provide a superb, all-round education that stimulates, challenges and captivates young minds, with opportunities for every child to excel, both inside and outside the classroom. When children leave Brighton College Prep Handcross at the end of Year 8, they are confident, resilient, academically curious and - most importantly - kind.
A Love of Learning
Academic excellence is at the very heart of a Brighton College education. We have the highest expectations for pupils, in terms of personal progress and academic attainment. This is achieved by fostering in each pupil a love of learning, curiosity about the world around them, and a deep intrinsic motivation to be the very best version of themselves.
Beyond the Classroom
Brighton College Prep Handcross inspires a love of sport, performing arts, and creativity.
Specialist sports lessons begin in Reception, with weekly fixtures from Year 3, promoting inclusivity, competition, and sportsmanship. From Nursery, pupils participate in music, drama and dance. Every child has lessons in music and drama each week, with our specialist teachers.
Art is taught in a modern design centre with a wonderful showcase gallery and its own garden space for outside creative work. As well as painting and drawing, pupils enjoy pottery, sewing, textile and photography. Design Technology sees pupils discover different stages of the design process, and the various tools, materials and techniques that will turn their ideas into reality!
Boarding
Boarding at Brighton College Prep Handcross is an incredibly special experience for each and every one of our pupils. Our supportive family environment promotes independence as well as a strong sense of belonging and assures our pupils that this is their home away from home.
From Year 4 (age 8), we offer a family-style boarding experience for either full, weekly or flexi boarders. We have a comprehensive bus service that picks up pupils from Sussex, Surrey and London. Our London service collects pupils from pick-up points across the city on a Monday morning and returns them on a Friday evening.
Within our beautiful boarding house, your child will make friends and memories that will last forever.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Performing Arts | Brighton College Prep Handcross
pageCache.text:
The Performing Arts
Specialist teaching in dance, drama and music is given to all pupils from Nursery to Year 8, helping to awaken a passion for performing arts.
The school is renowned for its high-quality theatre productions and concerts. Each child can participate in shows and concerts throughout the year, helping to build their confidence through music, dance and drama.
Our Performing Arts
Dance
Dance is introduced to pupils from Nursery as an enjoyable form of fitness and recreation. Dance is a key part of the Performing Arts Department where all pupils perform in our musical productions and is used as an increasingly important element to enhance storytelling and encourage both teamwork and self-expression on stage.
Pupils have the option to try a range of dance styles such as ballet, jazz, musical theatre and street dance. As well as our own dance clubs, we collaborate with external providers to expand the opportunities available for our pupils. Top Hat Stage School enhance our provision with fun Musical Theatre classes whilst Inspire Academy of Dance offer lessons for those wishing to focus on technique and work towards graded ISTD examinations.
Drama
Drama plays an integral role in the curriculum, with four spectacular productions a year and termly drama showcases. All pupils actively participate regardless of their level of experience or ability. Pupils are encouraged to get involved either on stage or behind the scenes, which provides a platform for them to showcase their skills and develop their confidence.
LAMDA lessons are increasingly popular. These lessons cover acting, verse and prose, public speaking, musical theatre and devising, and our pupils have a 100% pass rate.
Music
Most pupils play a musical instrument and are involved in a plethora of ensembles and bands. Our school orchestra, jazz band, brass band, string ensembles and choirs are all thriving, and they offer multiple opportunities for performances each term. All individual instrumental and vocal lessons are delivered by our team of excellent peripatetic teachers, who are all successful practising musicians outside of their teaching commitments.
The hard work and determination of our young musicians are evident in our 100% pass rate in the ABRSM, Trinity and Rockschool examinations.
Our Performances
Our performing arts departments work closely together to deliver a production programme, from ensemble pieces and instrumental and jazz concerts to drama recitals and dance Shows. Our events are a wonderful way for the school community to come together and share and enjoy the wonderful talent of our pupils.
The Creative Arts
Our creative arts curriculum is designed to foster the development of our pupils' imagination and self-expression, providing them with the tools and opportunities to explore and express themselves creatively.

Governors
The Board of Governors
Our Board of Governors possess amongst them a wealth of experience across a variety of disciplines. As our charity Trustees, they use their knowledge to maintain the best interests of the School, its property and its funds.
Chair of Governors: Miles TemplemanMiles Templeman is the former Director General of the Institute of Directors. Mr Templeman began his career as a marketing specialist and gained his pedigree leading such major consumer brands as Daz, Ribena and Lucozade, and was Marketing Director of Levis jeans. Miles is also on the Governing Body at Brighton College.
Adrian Ford - SafeguardingAdrian Ford is a Housemaster and Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead at Brighton College. Adrian grew up in South Wales and gained a History degree at Cardiff University before qualifying as a teacher. He has undertaken many roles in schools including a Director of Rugby, History and Politics Teacher and Housemaster of a co - educational House. He now runs School House at Brighton College as well as working on the Safeguarding Team.
Wendy Challen - EYFSEducated at Roedean, Wendy Challen graduated in Primary Education from the Froebel Institute at Roehampton University. Mrs Challen was the Head of Garden House School, Chelsea for 25 years and mentors new heads in post for IAPS and is a governor of a London maintained school and two independent prep schools in Sussex and Cambridge.
Emma Dobson MA - FinanceEmma Dobson is the Bursar of Brighton College. She joined the school in 2018 following 25 years in the Corporate sector as a Finance professional. Emma started her career with Unilever, a global consumer goods company, and spent a decade in the Netherlands fine-tuning her Dutch and cycling skills. Following several senior Finance Leadership positions in various multi-nationals, and too many trans-Atlantic flights, she moved to the independent school sector as a Bursar of Brighton College. Emma holds an MA in Natural Sciences from St John’s College, Cambridge
Jane Hamblett-Jahn - BoardingDirector of Boarding and Housemistress at Brighton College since 2014, Mrs Hamblett-Jahn gained her PGCE at the Institute of Education, University of London and prior to that her Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.), Business Law at Coventry University.
Shirley Harris BEd Hons - StaffShirley Harris qualified as a teacher in 1972 and later gained a BEd Hons degree based on primary Language and Literacy, specialising in school management in the final year. Mrs Harris completed Independent School Inspectorate training becoming a team inspector in 2002.
Jo-Anne Riley MA - Education and ComplianceJo-Anne Riley is the Deputy Headmistress (Academic) of Brighton College. Mrs Riley moved to Brighton College as Head of History in 1999 and was then appointed as Assistant Head Academic by Richard Cairns on his appointment as Head Master in 2006. Mrs Riley has written and introduced a new liberal arts course in Years 7 to 8 called ‘The Story of Our Land’ that replaces History, Geography and Religious Studies and covers the development of Britain from prehistoric times to the Enlightenment. Mrs Riley has been closely involved in the curriculum development of Brighton College Abu Dhabi.
Lady Serena Soames MA OxonSerena Soames has an MA in Human Sciences from Oxford University. Trained as an investment analyst, she has worked for charitable trusts supporting the preservation of unique buildings and environments, and promoting understanding of the countryside. She is a former Handcross parent and lives locally to Brighton College Prep Handcross.
Rishi Soni BSc, ACA, FCA - Health and SafetyCommercial Director of Brighton College International Schools, Mr Soni worked at KPMG for 12 years, where he qualified as a chartered accountant and spent 8 years in corporate finance working on a wide range of M&A transactions, fundraising and corporate restructurings. Mr Soni is responsible for assessing new international school opportunities and working with BCIS’s investors to plan and develop each overseas school.If you would like to contact a member of the Board of Governors please email the Clerk to the Governors (bursar@brightoncollegeprephandcross.co.uk), phone 01444 400 526, or write to the Clerk to the Governors at Brighton College Prep Handcross, London Road, Handcross, West Sussex, RH17 6HF.

pageCache.pageTitle: A Part of Society | Brighton College Prep Handcross
pageCache.text:
A Part of Society
We believe in nurturing kind and compassionate children who can positively impact the world.
Our commitment to giving back is reflected in the wide range of charitable initiatives we support, both locally and internationally.
Each year, our Charity Council , made up of pupils across the school, votes to support a local charity, helping raise awareness and funds through various events and activities. In recent years, we’ve proudly supported organisations such as Chestnut Tree House, Handcross Pantry, and Befriended, all of which do vital work within our Sussex community.
On a global level, we maintain a longstanding connection with Sparrows in South Africa, supporting their mission to care for and educate disadvantaged children and young adults.
We also take part in national and international appeals, including collecting and sending Christmas shoeboxes as part of Operation Christmas Child, bringing joy to children around the world during the festive season.
Through these activities, our pupils learn how to care for others, be kind, and make a real difference in the world.
Caring for our Planet
Our pupils understand the importance of environmental conservation from an early age. Our green pledge is embedded within our culture.
Our Forest School is committed to preserving the environment through sustainable practices, such as recycling, composting, and conserving resources.
Alongside Brighton College, we too have developed Beach School sessions, where pupils develop a deep understanding of the significance of accountability, compassion, and environmental awareness while participating in beach clean-up activities.
We offer many other ways for children to get involved with our pupil-led Eco Council, Gardening Club and Conservation Club. These enable children to gain a deeper understanding of sustainable practices and how they can make a difference to the world they live in.
Our Spaces
Our spaces provide the best environment for learning and growth.

Nursery
The perfect start to your child's educational journey at Brighton College Prep Handcross.
Our Nursery consists of 'Little Owls' for children aged 2-3 years and 'Wise Owls' for rising 4s. Our caring and inspiring teachers deliver a dynamic and engaging Early Years curriculum that captures a child's imagination and leads them on their journey of discovery and adventure. Nestled in our Secret Garden, it really is the perfect start to your child's education.
Our Spaces
Inspiring and engaging classrooms lead out to dedicated outdoor spaces for each Nursery class. There are chickens, mud kitchens, vegetable beds and a bespoke outdoor area, where the children can learn, play and grow through the seasons.
Being part of the Prep School also means the children can enjoy woodland walks and nature trails across our rural site, as well as weekly swimming in our heated pool and sports using our hall, astro and pitches.
Our Day
Every day, children are busily engaged in a range of activities, including cooking, gardening, art and craft, making music, roleplay and early reading and writing skills. Those children staying on for the afternoon are always in for a real treat with a brilliant programme of afternoon enrichment activities, which include dance, sporty tots, movement and mindfulness, Spanish, and Forest School - all with an exceptional team of specialist teachers.
There is a calm, purposeful air about the Nursery, as children develop skills and a love of learning. We want our children to become confident, happy, independent learners with inquiring minds.
We are very flexible in our Nursery, and can accommodate children for full or half-day sessions, with or without lunch. Our wraparound care offers care for your child from 7.45am to 6pm, 50 weeks of the year.
To view our Nursery Fees please blick the button below.
Our Mini Owls Toddler Group is the perfect way to explore our Nursery.
Before your child starts Little Owls, we invite you to join our Mini Owls Toddler Group. This runs every Tuesday afternoon and is the perfect way to get to know our staff and setting, ask questions and let your littles ones explore! If you'd like to join the sessions, please contact our Registrar.
Discover More

The Creative Arts
We believe that nurturing a child's creativity is essential to their education.
That's why we offer a broad range of art and design technology classes to all pupils from Nursery to Year 8. By encouraging our pupils to express themselves creatively, we help them build their skills in problem solving, critical thinking and visual literacy.
Whether children have an interest in painting, printmaking, pottery, sculpting, or working on graphic design and technology projects, we provide abundant opportunities for them to develop a lifelong appreciation of the creative arts.
Our Creative Arts
Art
Art is taught in our purpose-built, light and airy Art & Design Centre, with an incredible gallery to showcase our pupils superb work and its own relaxing garden space for outdoor artwork. The Art department is a truly creative environment for all our pupils. There is a kiln and a wheel available for pottery, a number of sewing machines available for textiles and state-of-the-art cameras available for photography.
Design and Technology
Design and Technology is taught in a spacious and well-equipped workshop. Pupils discover the different stages of the design process and the various tools, materials and techniques to turn their dreams and ideas into reality. Pupils work with plastics, metals and wood throughout the year groups.

pageCache.pageTitle: A Love of Learning | Brighton College Prep Handcross
pageCache.text:
A Love of Learning
Academic excellence is at the very heart of a Brighton College education.
We have the highest expectations for pupils, in terms of personal progress and academic attainment. This is achieved by fostering in each pupil a love of learning, curiosity about the world around them, and a deep intrinsic motivation to be the very best version of themselves.
We provide a superb, all-round education that stimulates, challenges and captivates young minds. When children leave Brighton College Prep Handcross at the end of Year 8, they are confident, resilient, academically curious and - most importantly - kind.
Our Subjects
English
From Nursery, we apply research-backed approaches to reading, including phonics, to ensure that all of our children are given strong foundations for reading, writing and spelling. As pupils develop their literacy skills, we seek to inspire them with a wide range of literature and to help them to apply this creativity in their own writing. As pupils move up through the prep school, our specialist and highly-experienced English teachers continue to support, stretch and challenge in class and beyond. This ensures that all of our learners are more than ready for the transition to senior school, including our academic scholars, who consistently achieve outstanding results in English.
Maths
From Nursery onwards, our Maths curriculum fosters numeracy, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills. Through hands-on activities, games, and interactive lessons, we inspire a love for numbers while building a deep understanding of mathematical concepts. Our vibrant and engaging classrooms create a positive learning environment where pupils develop confidence and a strong understanding of key topics, including number operations, fractions, decimals, percentages, algebra, geometry, measures, and statistics. This solid foundation sets the stage for future success in this essential subject.
Science
In Nursery, pupils are introduced to basic scientific concepts through interactive and engaging activities. As they progress through the year groups, they gradually incorporate biology, chemistry and physics in their scientific learning. From Year 3, pupils are taught in our state-of-the-art Science labs allowing hands-on experiments and practical activities. By the time they move to senior school, pupils are equipped to delve deeper into scientific fields and explore the interconnectedness of the natural world.
Computing and ICT
From Nursery onwards, our specialist-led computing and ICT curriculum builds a strong foundation in digital literacy. Pupils develop essential skills, including coding, presentation design, animation, 3D design and printing, and online safety. They engage in hands-on experiences such as flying drones, robotics and using a flight simulator, enhancing their learning through interactive technology. As a Google Reference School, we integrate Chromebooks seamlessly into lessons. Our approach ensures pupils are confident, creative, and responsible digital learners, prepared for the ever-evolving technological world.
Geography
Our Geography curriculum inspires curiosity about the world, its people, and the dynamic processes shaping it. Throughout their time at school, pupils explore both physical and human geography themes, developing an understanding of their environment and the wider world we are a part of. Through thoughtful discussion and research, pupils learn about current events and the geographical perspective they require, helping to understand the "where", "how" and "why". These skills lay the foundation for confident, informed learners, with valuable insights into the world around them
History
Our History curriculum encourages curiosity and critical thinking from a young age. It equips children with a chronological understanding of the past, from ancient civilizations to modern events, allowing them to contextualise the present. Interactive learning opportunities through themed days and visits to sites of historical significance bring the topic to life, whilst our bespoke 'Story of our Land' curriculum links the humanities subjects together and allows children to recognise the connections between each subject as part of their learning. Our History lessons also develop essential skills such as research, analysis, and effective communication through presentations and persuasive writing.
Art
From Nursery, our Art curriculum sets the stage for a lifelong love of creativity and expression. Our little artists learn about colours, shapes and different art materials through guided exploration. Pupils delve into pottery work using our kiln, printmaking, traditional painting techniques, sculpture work, photography and textiles. Our Art curriculum introduces pupils to a broad range of skills and materials to enable them the opportunity to make creative decisions as they mature into young artists. Our wonderful dedicated Art centre has a gallery to showcase their work, and a number of our Year 8 pupils go on to Senior School with an Art Scholarship.
Music
In Nursery, our young musicians begin their journey of musical discovery by exploring a variety of instruments and sounds. As they move up the school, they explore a broader repertoire that encompasses a wide range of music from different genres, eras and cultures. Pupils develop their listening, performing and composing skills through a myriad of practical tasks. Pupils regularly perform in concerts and recitals. We have an abundance of musical groups and choirs and there really is something for everyone! All pupils are encouraged to participate in instrumental lessons and performance activities.
Languages
From Nursery through to Year 8, all children learn Spanish as part of our core language curriculum. Mandarin is introduced from Year 1 and continues through to at least Year 6, offering pupils an early foundation in one of the world’s most widely spoken languages. In Year 6, pupils can also choose to study either French or Latin. Our vibrant language programme is enriched by a wide variety of cultural trips and immersive events, designed to bring the languages we teach to life. We celebrate international traditions and festivals throughout the year, including Chinese dancing workshops to mark Lunar New Year and a lively French Bake Off, where pupils can practise their language skills while enjoying French culinary culture.
Design Technology
Design Technology is taught from Year 3 onwards. Lessons take place in our dedicated DT workshop, where pupils are introduced to a variety of tools, materials, and processes in a safe and supportive environment. They learn to use hand tools and machines to create practical, well-crafted products, while also being introduced to modern technologies such as computer-aided design (CAD) and computer-aided manufacture (CAM). Our approach combines practical making with thoughtful design, encouraging pupils to plan, test, and refine their ideas.
Drama
Drama plays an integral role in the curriculum, with four major productions each year and termly showcases that highlight the talent and creativity of our pupils. These productions are fully inclusive, with every pupil encouraged to take part—regardless of experience or ability. This approach not only provides a platform for pupils to showcase their skills but also helps them build confidence and develop new talents. LAMDA lessons are increasingly popular and cover acting, verse and prose, public speaking, musical theatre and devising. Our results are outstanding, with 100% of those pupils receiving distinctions in the last year.
Physical Education and Games
Starting in Nursery with 'Sporty Tots', sport is an integral part of school life and provides a platform for children to explore new challenges, discover hidden talents and ultimately have fun, whilst maintaining a healthy lifestyle. All of our children play competitive sport from Year 3 through to Year 8 against other local prep and senior schools. We regularly host tournaments, swimming galas and cross country meets, so that our pupils have many opportunities to compete as part of their school teams. We also enter regional and national IAPS (The Independent Association of Prep Schools) tournaments across a variety of sports.
Religious Studies
We introduce our religious studies curriculum from Nursery. We foster pupils' spiritual, moral, social, cultural and intellectual growth by inspiring them to delve into the fundamental questions of belief and values that arise from various human experiences. Our curriculum incorporates elements of philosophical inquiry and ethical debate, helping pupils to develop critical thinking skills and a respectful appreciation of different perspectives. Children study a variety of world religions and cultural traditions, learning about their beliefs, practices, and historical significance. This broad approach not only deepens their knowledge but also fosters compassion, open-mindedness, and a sense of shared humanity.
Personal Social Health and Economic Education
PSHEE is a vibrant and essential part of the curriculum, thoughtfully tailored to each year group to support pupils’ personal growth and development. Wellbeing is woven into everyday school life, with mindfulness taught in fun, creative ways across all year groups. From yoga and mindfulness colouring to breathing exercises and journalling, pupils explore techniques that support emotional resilience and self-awareness. Each year, we shine a spotlight on wellbeing with our dedicated Mindfulness Week — a joyful celebration of everything we do to nurture happy, healthy minds.

Academic Life
A Love of Learning
Academic excellence is at the very heart of a Brighton College education. We have the highest expectations for pupils, in terms of personal progress and academic attainment. This is achieved by fostering in each pupil a love of learning, curiosity about the world around them, and a deep intrinsic motivation to be the very best version of themselves.
Around half our pupils move on to Brighton College every year, with others securing places at Senior Schools of their choice. 50% of pupils achieve scholarships to leading independent schools in Year 8 in a range of subjects inlcuding Academic, Music, Sport, Art and Design Technology.

Apply
The Application Process
Enquiring with us is the first stage of the admission process. To make your initial enquiry please contact our Registrar, Lisa Taylor, on 01444 400526 and choose option 1, email registrar@brightoncollegeprephandcross.co.uk or contact us below.
Following your enquiry we will send you an information pack and invite you to attend one of our Open Mornings or arrange a visit to the school to meet with the Headmaster, Mr Jonnie Besley, or our Head of Pre-Prep, Mrs Pennie Parry.
Applying for a place for your child is the next stage of the admissions process. If you would like to apply for a place, please complete the form by clicking the link at the bottom of this page, as soon as possible. This will register your interest for your child in the required year group. Once both the completed application form and payment have been received, your application will be processed. Please note that while an application is an important part of the process, it does not automatically guarantee a place.
Following an application, your child may be invited to either a Taster Day or an Assessment Morning (Years 3 - 8), so that we can carry out some informal assessments in Maths, English, and Non-Verbal Reasoning. For children being considered for a place in the Prep School the Assessment Morning may be followed by a ‘Taster Day’ (or overnight stay for a boarder) so that they can experience a day in the life of Brighton College Prep Handcross.
For a place in our Nursery & Pre-Prep, your child will be invited to join us for a Taster Session. The length of this session will depend on your child’s age.
Your child will be offered a place on the basis of a successful Assessment Morning and/or Taster Day. Parents are asked to complete an Acceptance Form based on our Terms and Conditions, to confirm acceptance of a place. At this time, parents are also requested to pay a deposit to guarantee the place. This deposit is refundable when your child leaves the school. Welcome and joining packs will be sent in the term before your child starts and you may also be invited to join us for any relevant information meetings.

Parents and Friends
Family is integral to the values of Brighton College Prep Handcross.
We frequently welcome parents and guardians to school. Whether it is for formal meetings such as parent consultations, special occasions like our Year 8 dinner, Prize Giving or weekly match teas after cheering on sports teams.
We understand that the opportunity to feel part of the community and form friendships is just as important for parents as it is for the children.
Friends of Handcross
The Friends of Handcross is a friendly association of Brighton College Prep Handcross parents, helping each other, having fun and supporting our very special school. The Friends Representatives, who are all parents, are here to help and to ensure that all parents get the most from the School.
Each year group has Year Reps. The role of the Reps is to welcome new parents into the school community. In addition, these invaluable volunteers maintain Whatsapp Groups for each Year Group to aid parents' organisation for school and social matters.
There are a large number of fun school activities throughout the year, such as the bonfire party, ball, quiz night, discos and the Christmas gift fair. Friends of Handcross events have helped make lasting memories and friendships for our school community. These events and other efforts have enabled the friends, in recent years, to help provide the funds for a Print-Making Press for the new Art and Design Centre, Cricket Scoreboards and a new PA System.
Anyone is welcome to get involved and all help is warmly received and much appreciated! It doesn’t matter how much or how little time you have to offer, the Friends of Handcross welcomes each and every parent’s participation.

Sport for All
Brighton College Prep Handcross offers one of the broadest sporting programmes among prep schools in Sussex.
Along with celebrating sporting excellence, our ethos is about sport for all.
We offer pupils a wide range of sporting opportunities, whatever their ability. Specialist sports lessons commence in Reception, with competitive matches starting in Year 3.
We value participation as equally important as performance. Engaging in sports nurtures teamwork, sportsmanship, discipline and resilience. It's not solely about winning or personal achievements but also about relishing the sport, contributing to the team, and acquiring valuable life skills that extend beyond the game.
A strong record exists in our core sports of athletics, cricket, football, hockey, netball, rugby, swimming and tennis, including success at county, regional and national levels.
Our Sports
Cricket
Cricket is taught as part of games from Reception to Year 8, with Years 3 to 8 playing competitive matches in the Summer term. Throughout the year, cricket is offered as a club to continue the progression of our young cricketers during the off season. A comprehensive and competitive fixture program is organised each year and with both indoor and outdoor nets and 11 cricket pitches across our spectacular 52-acre grounds.
Rugby
Rugby is one of the four major boys' sports at Brighton College Prep Handcross, with a strong tradition. Children will start basic handling, movement and understanding from Year 1 and then follow the RFU age-grade system with tag matches starting in Year 3. Managed contact matches will start from Year 4 for those wishing to do so, with also the opportunities to play touch rugby right up to Year 8.
Netball
As one of the major sports played at a competitive level, children from Year 1 to Year 8 are coached by our netball specialists in the basic fundamentals to advanced set plays and tactics. Our inclusive approach sees our children in Years 1 and 2 undertake weekly netball coaching, Year 3 play a 4-aside ‘Stinger Netball’ and Year 4 5-aside ‘Bee Netball’ formats before progressing to the standard 7-aside. Over the last year, 21 netball teams have represented the school, some of those competing in county and regional competitions.
Athletics
Athletics is one of the core sports at the heart of the PE curriculum and all pupils in Reception to Year 8 learn about and experience the various track and field events that the sport has to offer, differentiated at age-appropriate levels. Throughout the Summer Term, all pupils are furthering their understanding of the different events in preparation for Sports Day, competing to earn points for their Houses. Athletics clubs are also on offer for pupils in Years 3 to 8, in preparation for county, regional and national competitions. We are very proud of our National Athletes who have represented Sussex in a variety of track and field events.
Football
Football is for all at Brighton College Prep Handcross and the growth of the girls’ game has been particularly exciting over the last decade. As a core sport within our games curriculum, boys in Years 3 to 8 have their season in the Autumn term and girls in the Spring term. Years 1 and 2 also experience football within their games lessons. We are proud to host a variety of football tournaments throughout both the boys' and girls' seasons and for a variety of abilities and our ‘Be Trewe’ festivals are well renowned.
Hockey
Our hockey programme provides many opportunities for our pupils to develop and hone their skills from Reception to Year 2 through the PE curriculum and from Year 3 to 8 through the games curriculum and clubs. Both boys’ and girls’ hockey are one of the most successful sports at Brighton College Prep Handcross, with successes at county and regional level competitions.
Swimming
Swimming is a core part of PE for all children from Nursery to Year 8 and we strongly believe that swimming is not just a sport, it is a life skill. Pupils are taught by excellent swimming teachers who cover technique development across all four strokes (freestyle, backstroke, backstroke and butterfly) as well as advanced skills such as diving and tumble turns. In Years 7 and 8, pupils also have the opportunity to experience water polo, lifesaving and personal survival. Swimming squad training is on offer for Years 3 to 8, for advanced training and regularly participate in swimming galas and IAPS competitions.
Physical Education
Physical Education is taught by our team of specialists from Nursery to Year 8. Through a broad and varied physical education curriculum the pupils gain opportunities to not just develop skills and sport-specific understanding, but also to learn about teamwork, sportsmanship, leadership, perseverance, communication and resilience. This encompasses a range of sports from athletics to swimming, from volleyball to badminton, gymnastics to dance and pop lacrosse to health-related fitness, to name but a few! The aim is not just to instil a love of being physically active, but also a love of learning beyond the classroom.
Our Sporting Spaces
All our pupils benefit from the use of our outstanding sports facilities including a wealth of football. cricket and rugby pitches, all-weather pitches, athletic tracks, netball and tennis courts, swimming pool, climbing wall, cricket nets and even our own 6-hole golf course!
Our 52-acres of land contain cricket, rugby and football pitches.
Our full size astro pitch is an ideal space for hockey, football and other sports.
Our heated 17m swimming pool is used from nursery for weekly swimming lessons and swimming galas.
A wonderful 6-hole golf course is within our grounds and features a putting green for extra practice!

Trips
We believe learning extends far beyond the classroom.
Our varied programme of school trips offers pupils incredible opportunities to explore new places, develop new skills, and make unforgettable memories.
From the excitement of our ski trip and the challenge of conquering the Three Peaks, to enriching cultural experiences such as the Year 8 Leavers’ trip to Spain, our trips are thoughtfully planned to inspire, educate, and broaden pupils’ horizons.
We offer dedicated language-immersion visits to support and enhance pupils’ learning in Spanish and Mandarin, bringing classroom learning to live through real-world experiences.
Pupils also enjoy leadership-focused outdoor expeditions, including camping, hiking, climbing and summiting in Snowdonia, building resilience and teamwork in stunning natural settings. Our close relationship with Brighton College provides special opportunities too – such as meeting the England Rugby Team and taking part in an immersive drama day in their brand new Cairns Theatre.
We make the most of our location with regular visits to museums, London landmarks, Brighton Marina, and other local cultural hotspots, ensuring pupils are exposed to a wide range of experiences. Every trip is carefully curated to complement our curriculum and nurture confidence, independence, and curiosity in every child.
Our Trips
Our trip calendar is packed with unforgettable experiences. Highlights include the French Ski Trip, stepping back in time to the WWI Battlefields in the Somme and Ypres, and tackling the The Great Escape in Shropshire.
Pupils also enjoy hiking the South Downs, conquering the Twin Peaks Challenge, making a splash with Yellowave water sports, and summiting Snowdon. The year ends on a high with our Year 8 celebration trip, most recently a week was spent in Barcelona — a true celebration of adventure and achievement!

Beyond the Classroom
Our children know there is a whole world beyond the classroom.
Brighton College Prep Handcross inspires a love of sport, performing arts, and creativity.We understand the importance of flexibility for families, so offer an extended day and over 100 clubs during lunchtimes, before and after school. We encourage every pupil to participate in our activities programme and make the most of the wonderful opportunities that surround them.
Sport for All
As part of one of the leading sporting schools in England, Brighton College Prep Handcross is exceptionally well-equipped to introduce children to sport and awaken a love of physical activity.
The Performing Arts
We encourage our children to participate in the arts to foster their creativity and individuality. This enlivens and complements their school life in a very special way.
The Creative Arts
Our creative arts curriculum is designed to foster the development of our pupils' imagination and self-expression, providing them with the tools and opportunities to explore and express themselves creatively.
Trips and Clubs
Brighton College Prep Handcross offers exciting trips throughout the year and over 100 clubs to choose from! We also provide flexible care for up to 51 weeks of the year.
